Sam P.: Hey team — StratusBank (gov account) asked whether we should do PrivateLink or VPC peering for their Private deployment POC. They require mutual TLS between their on‑prem proxy and our connector, and strict firewall allowlists. Can we outline tradeoffs and an actionable POC path?
Alex C.: Quick take: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) usually easier for cross-account + least blast radius. VPC peering is fine within same org/region but doesn't support endpoint-based access control as cleanly. For mTLS, we can terminate client certs at our NLB or require mTLS at the connector app.
Maria G.: Also note GovCloud has special endpoints and sometimes different ENI behaviors. PrivateLink avoids routing changes on their side — they only need to allow outbound to our interface endpoint IPs.
Priya R.: If they insist on preserving source IP and doing deep packet inspection, peering + transit may be required. PrivateLink NATs traffic at the endpoint (source becomes interface ENI). Need to confirm what their IDS/IPS expects.
Chris L.: For mutual auth we can support two patterns: 1) TLS at NLB with client cert validation (managed certs uploaded to NLB via ACM/private certs) 2) mTLS inside the TCP connection to the connector service (app level). Pattern 1 offloads validation but requires them to upload CA chain or our cert to their side.
Sam P.: Ok — firewall rules. They want explicit port list and IP ranges to provide to their security team. Can we give a minimal allowlist for PrivateLink and for peering?
Alex C.: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) model — customer allows outbound to the interface endpoint ENIs (AWS provides ENI IPs in their VPC). From their on‑prem to their VPC you just need the VPN/Direct route. On our side, we require inbound from the PrivateLink ENIs to the connector NLB on 443 (or 8443). Example SG on our side:
```
Type: TCP
Port: 443
Source: <customer-privatelink-eni-cidrs>
```
Note: ENI IPs are dynamic per AZ; we'll provide the current set for the POC and update if AZs change.
Maria G.: For VPC peering path (if they peer their VPC to ours or transit via TGW), ports are the same but the source will be their VPC CIDR blocks. No NAT at AWS peering level so source IP is preserved. Example ingress SG for peering:
```
Type: TCP
Port: 443
Source: 10.12.0.0/16  # customer's spoke VPC
```
Also need to ensure route tables have the peering route and no overlapping CIDRs.
Priya R.: Ops note: If they have TLS inspect middleboxes that break client cert exchange, prefer NLB termination + our verifying upstream cert. If TLS inspect is in place, app mTLS will fail. Ask them whether TLS intercept is present.
Chris L.: POC checklist I recommend we share with them (short):
- Confirm deployment mode (PrivateLink vs Peering) and AWS partition (aws-us-gov vs aws).
- Provide customer VPC CIDRs + on‑prem egress IPs (for peering case) OR allowlist of PrivateLink ENIs (we'll supply).
- Decide cert model: customer-provided CA for client certs or Redwood-managed certs.
- Confirm ports: 443 (TLS) port for API/connector; 22 only for SSH bastion if needed for debug (not recommended).
- Agree on rollback/fallback: if PrivateLink fails, can we fallback to internet egress via their NAT? (usually not allowed in gov setups).
Sam P.: Good. Infra Bot — generate current POC IP set we can send to customer? @Infra Bot can we get ENI list and a short JSON of ports? :pray:

Infra Bot: ENI_IPS: ["10.0.48.23","10.0.52.11","10.1.12.9"]  NLB_TARGETS: ["34.201.11.5","34.201.11.6"]  PORTS: ["443"]
Maria G.: I'll draft the security email: include the SG snippets, the cert options, and a note about GovCloud partition. Will ask for their network runbook contact and their TLS inspection policy.
Chris L.: If they want IP stability for allowlist, we can offer reserved EIPs in front of the NLB for Dedicated customers — raise with sales if they want that for the POC.
Sam P.: Next steps for sales thread: I'll request customer's network contact, ask for their TLS intercept doc, and send the SG/ENI snapshot. Can someone on eng side own the cert validation flow docs? @Alex C. you?
Alex C.: I can own cert flow docs and a tiny example for their security team showing NLB client cert config and app mTLS fallback. Will post later today. :thumbsup:
Maria G.: I'll prepare the email template and attach the Infra Bot snapshot.
Sam P.: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll ping StratusBank and update this thread with their network contact and the requested artifacts. :rocket:
